header:
Date: 2026-08-19 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~49m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CISO, Oxford National Bank), Marcus Doyle (Head of Cloud Ops), Priya Singh (Compliance)
summary: Discovery focused on data residency and compliance requirements for deploying Redwood inference. Customer preference is strong for data residency in EU and US, strict audit/logging controls, and options for Dedicated or Private deployments. Action items agreed: send security artifacts, schedule technical deep dive/benchmark, share VPC/network diagrams and pilot pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Network connectivity: VPC peering, private link
Latency vs cost concerns for Dedicated capacity
transcript:
00:00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samira Patel from Redwood. Quick roll call?
00:00:05 Speaker 2 (Laura): Hi, Laura Chen, CISO at Oxford National.
00:00:07 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Marcus Doyle, Head of Cloud Ops.
00:00:09 Speaker 4 (Priya): Priya Singh, Compliance.
00:00:12 Speaker 2 (Samira): And Ethan Cole, our solutions engineer, is here from Redwood. Ethan, do you want to say hi?
00:00:16 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Yep, hi all. I'll be the technical lead on follow-ups, happy to dig into architecture and logs and benchmarks.
00:00:25 Speaker 1 (Samira): Great. Agenda — quick qual on current stack and requirements, dig into residency and logging, then outline deployment options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and next steps.
00:00:36 Speaker 2 (Laura): Sounds good. To be upfront, we have strict residency needs — our retail banking PII for European customers must stay in EU. We also have a subset of US customer data that has to remain in the US.
00:00:51 Speaker 3 (Marcus): From an ops perspective we need network controls — VPC peering or private link, no internet-egress for inference traffic ideally. Also we want control over audit logs and retention windows.
00:01:03 Speaker 4 (Priya): Compliance also needs attestations: SOC 2, ISO 27001, and we have internal policies about logging retention and redaction of sensitive fields.
00:01:12 Speaker 1 (Samira): Understood — that's a very common pattern. Quick Q: are you currently using any hosted LLM APIs?
00:01:18 Speaker 2 (Laura): We have experiments with a couple of cloud providers but nothing in production. Mainly concerned that data sent to hosted endpoints could be logged or used for model training.
00:01:29 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Good point. For Redwood hosted, we offer region-located endpoints and contractual assurances around data usage — no customer data used for training. For higher restrictions we have Dedicated and Private options where data never leaves customer-controlled networks.
00:01:43 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Can you clarify the differences? Like network path and who has access to logs?
00:01:48 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Sure. Hosted — easiest, public API endpoints but you can pin region (EU/US) and we provide encryption at rest and in transit. Logs are retained by Redwood per the tenant settings; you can request reduced retention or redaction. Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, still managed by Redwood but in a logically isolated tenancy and you can restrict admin access via RBAC and SSO. Private — customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem) where inference nodes live inside your network, we provide the software bundle. In Private, logs and KV cache can be configured to stay in your environment.
00:02:26 Speaker 2 (Laura): For us, Private is ideal but there's procurement time and ops overhead. What's the typical timeline?
00:02:31 Speaker 1 (Samira): Private deployments take longer — usually a few months with procurement and security review. Dedicated can be onboarded faster, often weeks, and gives a balance of isolation with less operational burden.
00:02:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): About logs — we need immutable audit logs for requests and admin actions for at least seven years for some regs, but we also want the ability to redact user-submitted PII in transcripts. How does Redwood handle that?
00:02:55 Speaker 5 (Ethan): We support configurable log retention and log redaction pipelines. For Hosted and Dedicated, we can apply on-ingest redaction rules to strip or mask defined fields (SSNs, account numbers). For Private, you control the pipeline, so redaction and retention are entirely in your hands. Note though immutable audit logs often implies write-once storage — we can support syslog/S3 export with object-lock policies if you need WORM retention.
00:03:22 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Ok, and key management — can we bring our own keys (BYOK) for encryption at rest?
00:03:27 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Yes. For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK/HSM integrations). For Hosted we offer BYOK in some regions via partner KMS integrations — we'll include specifics in the security pack.
00:03:40 Speaker 2 (Laura): GDPR-wise — we need clear data flows and ability to demonstrate data minimization and purpose limitation. We also may need a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with EU-specific clauses.
00:03:51 Speaker 1 (Samira): Absolutely. We have a standard DPA with EU SCCs and can add bespoke clauses for enterprise deals. We'll send the DPA and our privacy/security whitepaper.
00:03:59 Speaker 4 (Priya): Regarding access control: we need SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC scoped to teams, and full admin audit. Any limits there?
00:04:09 Speaker 5 (Ethan): We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and granular RBAC — you can control route-level permissions, who can create models or override routing policies. Audit trails include admin actions.
00:04:20 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Network connectivity specifics — do you support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, or Transit Gateway?
00:04:26 Speaker 5 (Ethan): We support VPC peering and PrivateLink for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be accessed over PrivateLink in some regions; otherwise VPN or peering for Private. We'll share sample VPC diagrams.
00:04:37 Speaker 2 (Laura): We also have a question on logging sensitivity — sometimes transcripts include customer full PII in prompts. Do you have redaction tools that operate on prompt-side before storage?
00:04:47 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Yes — we can run PII detection and mask on ingest. There's a performance tradeoff but we can tune it. Redwood Optimize also has suggestions for prefix caching that avoid storing full user inputs in logs when not necessary.
00:04:59 Speaker 1 (Samira): Also wanted to call out fallbacks — for strict compliance customers, we often recommend a Dedicated deployment with region pinning plus a short pilot to validate latency and logging. That often addresses procurement concerns quicker than full Private.
00:05:12 Speaker 4 (Priya): What about e-discovery and legal hold? If regulators request data, how quickly can logs be exported with chain-of-custody?
00:05:20 Speaker 5 (Ethan): We can export logs to your controlled S3 or SIEM. For chain-of-custody we provide signed exports and timestamped audit trails; for high security you'd want Private so exports are fully under your control.
00:05:33 Speaker 3 (Marcus): On performance: Dedicated versus Hosted — what kind of latency uplift should we expect if we go Dedicated in our region? Our apps are latency-sensitive for interactive chat.
00:05:43 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Dedicated deployed in the same region will have comparable latency to Hosted. Differences come from model variant selection and batching settings. We can tune kernel selection and batching to keep p95 latency within SLOs. We'll propose baseline configs for your concurrency patterns and run a benchmark.
00:05:59 Speaker 2 (Laura): Any references — banks you've worked with with similar constraints?
00:06:03 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes — we've onboarded several regional banks with Dedicated and Private: we can share anonymized case studies and benchmark numbers.
00:06:11 Speaker 4 (Priya): About incident response — we need runbooks and RTO/RPO expectations if there's an outage affecting inference.
00:06:18 Speaker 5 (Ethan): We provide incident playbooks and SLAs for Dedicated customers; Private customers retain responsibility for RTO/RPO but we offer support tiers and runbook templates.
00:06:28 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Can we do a short pilot — say two weeks of traffic — to evaluate latency and logs before committing?
00:06:33 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes, a pilot on Dedicated capacity is typical. We'll propose a pilot scope: 2-4 reserved GPUs for two weeks, defined test corpus, and logging config to validate redaction and retention.
00:06:47 Speaker 4 (Priya): Cost question — Dedicated looks expensive. Are there hybrid options?
00:06:51 Speaker 5 (Ethan): You can mix: Hosted for low-risk traffic, Dedicated for regulated EU/US customer data, and Private for the highest risk. We can also provide autoscaling and burst options to optimize cost.
00:07:03 Speaker 2 (Laura): We need procurement and legal to review security artifacts before any pilot.
00:07:08 Speaker 1 (Samira): Understood — we'll send the SOC2 and ISO attestation, DPA, data flow diagrams, and a deployment options matrix. Ethan will prepare a technical packet for your security team.
00:07:18 Speaker 5 (Ethan): I'll include sample VPC peering configs, KMS integration notes, and log export examples to S3 with object lock.
00:07:26 Speaker 3 (Marcus): One more: can benchmarks include worst-case concurrency and token costs so we can estimate monthly run rates?
00:07:32 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Yes — benchmark plan will measure latency under expected concurrency, token throughput, and cost per 1M tokens for chosen model variant and quantization profiles. We'll include quantization and batching recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
00:07:46 Speaker 4 (Priya): For GDPR DSARs — if a customer requests deletion, how do we ensure all traces are removed from logs and backups?
00:07:53 Speaker 5 (Ethan): DSARs are supported; for Hosted/Dedicated we can delete records from active logs and provide attestations, but backups/immutable storage may need special handling — Private gives you direct control. We'll include DSAR procedure in the security docs.
00:08:07 Speaker 1 (Samira): Ok let's recap action items and next steps.
00:08:12 Speaker 2 (Samira): Samira: I'll send SOC2/ISO attestation, DPA draft, and the deployment matrix by 2026-08-20.
00:08:18 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Ethan: I'll prepare the SE packet with VPC diagrams, KMS notes, benchmark plan, and sample configs by 2026-08-23.
00:08:24 Speaker 2 (Laura): Laura: we'll share our list of required regions and a short regulatory checklist by 2026-08-22.
00:08:31 Speaker 4 (Priya): Priya: I'll coordinate with legal and let you know if they need an NDA.
00:08:36 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Marcus: I'll provision a test VPC for the benchmark week and point to whitelisted IPs.
00:08:42 Speaker 1 (Samira): Great. Schedule — can we pencil in a technical deep dive the week of 2026-08-24?
00:08:48 Speaker 2 (Laura): That works for us.
00:08:50 Speaker 5 (Ethan): I'll propose a couple slots in the calendar.
00:08:53 Speaker 1 (Samira): Anything else?
00:08:55 Speaker 2 (Laura): One small note: bank execs will want a clear justification for cost vs risk — if you can include comparison slides that map Hosted/Dedicated/Private to risk levels that would help.
00:09:04 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll include that in the deck. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the documents.
00:09:10 Speaker 2 (Laura): Thanks.
00:09:12 Speaker 3 (Marcus): Thanks all.
00:09:14 Speaker 4 (Priya): Thanks.
00:09:16 Speaker 5 (Ethan): Bye.
00:09:18 Meeting end (call lasted ~49m)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes rendered as "K V cache", "PrivateLink" as "Privatelink"). Speakers sometimes abbreviated. Crossover when multiple people speak quickly.
